raw_response:
Well, it's late April now, time to get my hands in the soil. I've been farming this land for 30 years — started when I was 22, right after I finished middle school. Back then we mostly did wheat and maize, but about 8 years ago my brother-in-law in Taoli village told me stevia was earning good money, so I switched most of my land over. Now I've got 4.1 mu total: 2.5 mu for stevia, which is my main cash crop, and 1.6 mu for cotton, mostly for family use — my wife still likes to have our own cotton for quilts, and the cottonseed oil saves us buying vegetable oil.

Seven people in my household, but my son and his wife work at the textile factory in Handan, and my daughter is in Shijiazhuang. That off-farm money is what keeps us going, honestly. It's me (52), my wife, and my old mother at home, plus my younger son who helps when he's not doing construction jobs. So it's family labor for the farm, no hired hands — can't afford 100 yuan a day for laborers, not on 4 mu.

**Stevia (2.5 mu)**

The seedlings need to go in now — it's April 20, and if I wait too long the growing season gets short. I buy chengguang seedlings from the nursery, about 7,000 plants per mu. Cost me 600 yuan per mu this year, same as last year more or less. I thought about buying cheaper ones from the market, but last year my neighbor did that and half his seedlings died. Better to pay a bit more for reliable stock.

For fertilizer, the soil here is decent but I always put down basal before planting. I use the general compound fertilizer, 15-15-15, about 50 kg per mu. That's 100 jin — I know it in jin, that's how I measure. I also spread about 250 kg of chicken manure per mu that I get from Old Wang down the road. He sells it cheap, 60 yuan for a cartload, and it keeps the soil loose. The extension technician told us last year that stevia needs about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, and with the compound plus the manure I'm about right there. I'll topdress twice: once around 40 days after planting with urea, about 15 kg per mu, and again at 70 days with another 25 kg of compound. Three fertilizer applications total.

Irrigation — well water, border flood. It's expensive, electricity for the pump keeps going up. I'll irrigate 5 times: right after transplanting, then at about 30 days, 60 days, and twice more before harvest in late August. If we get good rain I might skip the third one, but stevia needs moisture for the leaves, so I don't like to gamble.

For pesticides, I keep it light. Stevia buyers are picky about residues. I'll spray herbicide once after planting, that's it. No insecticide unless I see something serious — last year I didn't need any.

Tillage is rotary, I hire Old Li's tractor — 50 yuan per mu, he does it in an hour. For labor, it's all family. Planting the seedlings takes about 3 days for 2.5 mu with me and my wife bending down all day. Weeding is the killer — 3 or 4 times through the season, about 12 days total. Harvesting in late August, another 5 days to cut and dry. So about 20 family days for the stevia.

Yield? Last year I got about 580 kg per mu, dried. This year the soil looks about the same, no major disease last year, so I'm hoping for 600 kg per mu. If the price stays around 500 yuan per jin... well, I shouldn't count my chickens before they hatch. Let's say I expect 600 kg per mu.

**Cotton (1.6 mu)**

Cotton is simpler. I plant late April, harvest September-October. I save some seed but I also buy 1.25 kg of fresh seed per mu — about 40 yuan. Rotary till with Li's tractor again. Basal fertilizer: 50 kg of compound 15-15-15 per mu. One topdressing of urea, about 12 kg per mu, when the plants start flowering.

Irrigate 3 times — cotton can take a bit of drought, but with only 1.6 mu I can afford the water. If it rains well in July, maybe only twice.

Pesticide: if I see bollworms, I'll spray once. Otherwise nothing. Cotton doesn't need much spraying if you watch it.

Labor: planting 1 day, weeding 2 days, harvest and picking about 3 days — 6 family days total.

Yield expectation: about 250 kg per mu of seed cotton. Not great money, but it's for family use mostly.

**Budget and tradeoffs**

My biggest constraint is cash. The stevia seedlings alone cost 1,500 yuan. Add fertilizer for both crops, tillage, irrigation electricity, and I'm spending about 3,100 yuan this season. That's a big chunk of what I have saved. I thought about putting more fertilizer on the stevia — maybe get 650 kg per mu — but that would cost another 200 yuan and I'd rather have that cash in case my mother's medicine costs go up. You never know. Last year I put a bit more on and the yield barely changed, so this year I'm sticking to what worked.

The other tradeoff is labor versus money. I could hire people for weeding and save my back, but at 100 yuan a day, that's 3 or 4 days of stevia weeding — 400 yuan — and I'd rather do it myself and keep the money. My wife and I are still strong enough, though at 52 I feel it more than I used to.

I also thought about dropping the cotton and planting all stevia. But cotton gives us oil and filling for quilts, and my wife insists. Plus, if the stevia price crashes, at least we have cotton. Diversification — my father taught me that.

So that's the plan. Nothing fancy, nothing new. Stick with what works, watch the costs, pray for rain in July.
